title: A / an, the and zero article 3
subtitle: books / the books; on Saturday / on a Saturday
summary: Choose between the and zero article with plural and uncountable nouns, with days, seasons and times of day, and with means of transport.

left.label: Zero article - talking generally
left.text: With plural and uncountable nouns we use no article when we have no definite people or things in mind.
examples: The government has promised not to tax **books**. (= books generally)
**Music** played an important part in his life. (= music generally)

right.label: the - the listener knows which ones
right.text: We use the when we assume the listener or reader will understand who or what we mean, or when other words in the noun phrase make the reference specific.
examples: **The books** have arrived. (= the books you ordered)
I thought **the music** used in the film was the best part.

lesson.heading: Holidays and days of the week
lesson.text: We use zero article with the names of holidays and special times of the year: **Easter, Ramadan, New Year's Day**. With days of the week the article changes the meaning.

examples.text: They came on **a Saturday** as far as I can remember.
examples.note: we are only interested in the day of the week, not which particular Saturday

examples.text: They came on **the Saturday** after our party.
examples.note: a particular Saturday, and we say which one

lesson.heading: Seasons and New Year
lesson.text: With **winter, summer, spring, autumn** and **New Year** (the holiday period) we can use either zero article or *the*. We use *the* when it is understood, or when we go on to specify, which one we mean.

examples.text: In **(the) summer** I try to spend as much time as I can in the garden.
I'd like to go skiing in **the autumn**.
I first went skiing in **the spring** of 2002.
I'll see you again in **the New Year**.
examples.note: = near the beginning of next year

examples.text: That was **a winter** I'll never forget.
examples.note: compared with other winters it was unforgettable

examples.text: That was **the winter** we went to Norway.
examples.note: a statement about one particular winter

lesson.heading: Times of the day
lesson.text: We use zero article with **midnight, midday** and **noon**, and either *dawn* or *the dawn*. We use **the + morning / afternoon / evening** for a day that is understood or already specified.

examples.text: If possible, I'd like it finished by **midday**. **Midnight** couldn't come quickly enough.
He got back into bed and waited for **(the) dawn**.
I enjoyed **the morning**, but in **the afternoon** the course was boring.
**Morning** is the time I work best.
examples.note: = mornings in general; The morning ... is also possible

examples.text: I'll be there by **(the) morning / evening**.
examples.note: but ... by the afternoon, not by afternoon
more usual than all the morning

examples.text: 'You look upset.' 'Yes, I've had **a terrible morning**.'

lesson.heading: by bus or take the bus?

left.label: by + zero article
left.text: We often use by + zero article to talk about means of transport and communication.
examples: I generally go **by bus** to work.
go / travel **by car / taxi / plane / train / air / sea**

right.label: the / a + the noun itself
right.text: When the vehicle or message is a thing rather than a method, it takes an ordinary article.
examples: I generally take **the bus** to work.
It's raining, so I think I'll take **the car**.
I got **an email** from Carla yesterday.

lesson.text: For plural and uncountable nouns the question is never *is it countable?* but *does my listener already know which ones I mean?* If yes, use *the*; if you mean the whole class, use no article.

exercises.prompt: Does each gap need zero article (a general reference) or the (a specific one)?

items.text: ___ Children as young as ten are working in the clothing industry.
While you're painting the sitting room, I'll take ___ children over to the park.
Around 60% of the labour force in the county is supported by ___ agriculture.
As the soil quality deteriorated, so too did ___ agriculture on which the region depended.
It is said that ___ money is the root of all evil.
I've left ___ money I owe you on your desk.
Animals fear ___ fire more than anything else.
It isn't known how ___ fire started.

exercises.prompt: Around the world ___ are being threatened by rising sea levels.
exercises.explanation: A general reference to islands everywhere, so zero article.

exercises.prompt: ___ off the east coast of Malaysia are beautiful.
exercises.explanation: The phrase off the east coast of Malaysia makes the reference specific, so the.

exercises.prompt: I've been working in the garden all ___ and my back aches.
exercises.explanation: all afternoon is more usual than all the afternoon.

exercises.prompt: A: Can you remember when we last saw Alex? B: It was ___ in June, I think.
exercises.explanation: a + day of the week when we are only interested in which day it was, not which particular Sunday.

exercises.statement: A: Shall we go out walking on the Sunday? B: No, I'm busy this weekend.
exercises.explanation: Shall we go out walking on Sunday? For next Sunday we use zero article.

exercises.prompt: I got my laptop on July 15th last year. I remember because it was also ___ day I passed my driving test.
exercises.explanation: The following clause specifies which day, so the is needed.

exercises.prompt: A: I haven't seen Subin for months. B: He's been away in South Africa for ___.
exercises.explanation: We use the because it is understood which winter is meant.

exercises.prompt: A: Do you remember when Mateo did all the cooking? B: Of course. It was ___ the rest of us had flu.
exercises.explanation: We go on to say which Christmas it was, so the is used.

exercises.prompt: A: Remember when Lars and Ella had that terrible row? B: How could I forget? That was ___ I wouldn't want to go through again.
exercises.explanation: That was + a / an + noun + modifying phrase says what made that day special compared with others.

exercises.prompt: Complete each sentence with the right phrase.

pairs.left: The train was cancelled, so I had to come ...
It's raining, so I think I'll take ...
The quickest way to get in touch with him is ...

exercises.prompt: Research has found that living plants are efficient at absorbing pollutants in ___.
exercises.explanation: Here we mean the air around us - a specific, understood thing - so the.
